Always let your injector know of adverse effects/complications so they can Inject other muscles & improve it! And go to your follow up appointments!

We all have to learn somehow b
transcript: I want to preface this by saying that this does not mean that you had a bad Botox job. It certainly can be due to injection technique, but every single experienced injector in the best in the world have had several eyelid ptosis and any injector that tells you otherwise is either lying or a brand new injector. However, what does really matter when going to an injector is not to ensure that they've never had any complications occur before because that's actually not a good sign. You want an injector with that kind of experience and knowledge of how to treat those complications if and when they occur, but you want to ensure that your injector is being upfront and transparent on the front end about the risk of complications, what that would look like when you start to see these complications occur and how they would manage them. An eyelid ptosis occurs because neurotoxin diffuses into this levator palpebrae superioris muscle that works to keep the lid open. We know that neurotoxin is an opposite drug, meaning it makes the muscle do the opposite of what it naturally does. So if that muscle naturally keeps the lid open, it makes sense that toxin would do the opposite and try to close that lid, also causing the unaffected eye to work harder and overcompensate and recruit. Now for this muscle that can't work as hard, which is why her other eye, the unaffected side, appears to be bulging or bug eye. And this can happen due to extrusion force, so how quickly the volume in the syringe is being pushed, also the direction of the needle. It typically happens when we're injecting the lateral corrugators. Depth matters if we're too deep, if the needle is directed towards that frame in. So also lying down flat within four hours, exercising within 24 hours, and massaging or manipulating the injection site within four weeks of a tox treatment before it has had a chance to fully settle can all increase the risk of acquiring an eyelid ptosis. So I treated this patient by injecting two units originally in the pre-torsal muscle here. So the pre-torsal muscle is one of the muscles that works to close the lid, meaning it will have the opposite effect and help to open the lid. So then I saw her a week later post pre-torsal injection and I decided to inject four more units into that pre-torsal muscle here and a few more units in the orbicularis oculi muscle. And this was her improvement after one week. And this was her eyelid after two weeks. Here is the side by side in two weeks post ptosis. …[truncated]

creator: DrDrayzday
title: Why Tretinoin Stops Working
caption:
Does tretinoin really stop working over time? Dermatologist Dr. Dray explains why your skin becoming more tolerant of tretinoin does not necessarily mean the retinoid has stopped working.

If acne comes back while using tretinoin, there may be other explanations, including changes in hormones, acne severity, skincare routines, or how consistently the medication is being used. Tretinoin and other topical retinoids can also be used as maintenance treatments to help prevent acne from returning.

Dr
transcript: What's the deal? Why is my tretinoin no longer working? Did my skin become resistant to it? This is something a lot of people end up encountering when it comes to using a topical retinoid. The benefits that they observed in the beginning, maybe they've observed them for a while. All of a sudden, it doesn't cut it in. Your acne, it's breaking out. So does this stop working? No. Topical retinoids do not stop working. Nor does your skin develop tolerance to or resistance against. Topical retinoids work by binding to certain receptors and skin cells and influencing the genes that are expressed, ultimately playing a role in how they act. And that doesn't change with ongoing use. What is more likely is that your skin condition is no longer well controlled by this topical alone. In the case of acne, this is not actually unusual. Acne is influenced by your hormones, which can change throughout your lifetime. It doesn't mean that this stop working. It just means that perhaps you need to see your dermatologist because maybe you need additional treatment in order to now exert control above and beyond a topical retinoid.

current.subject: does tretinoin stop working
current.claim: Tretinoin doesn't stop working or build resistance; your acne, often hormonal, has outgrown topical control.
